model_plan.confirmation: Use cost_reduction because it directly measures setup savings against the current engine; its baseline is zero, so 0.02 represents a minimum worthwhile 2% reduction. Before final proposal draws, freeze the two assembly policies, allowed parameter variation, selection rules and analysis. Obtain 32 independent program-proposal draws per policy, pairing shared structural settings across policies to preserve the escape contrast. Include a model-call-budget-matched original-proposer control with the same 256-evaluation execution cap. Keep generation, scoring, shadow, verification and final-generation workloads separate; freeze every evaluated program before exposing final workloads. Evaluate all frozen programs on the same 128 independent final workloads, balanced across four families, using the host's fixed workload seeds. Audit cycle validity, primitive compliance and the full evaluation budget, including kicks. Estimate mean paired gains against baseline and policy-to-policy contrasts using a two-way bootstrap over independent proposal draws and shared workloads, preserving pairing and family balance. Use simultaneous 95% confidence intervals for the two baseline comparisons; support a worthwhile-effect claim only when its lower bound exceeds 0.02. Report the policy contrast, original-proposer control comparison, family results and host-native decision separately. Do not select a winner or claim an improvement before execution.

hypotheses.claim: Nearest-neighbor schedules leave accessible local improvements; targeted greedy search can exceed a mean absolute cost_reduction of 0.02 without uphill exploration.
hypotheses.experiment: Use a greedy-only assembly policy with expensive-transition search followed by systematic polishing. Executable reference program: {"stages":[{"operators":["relocate","swap"],"sampling":"expensive","acceptance":"improve","temperature":0,"cooling":0,"restart":"continue","kick":0,"weight":60},{"operators":["relocate","swap","reverse"],"sampling":"scan","acceptance":"improve","temperature":0,"cooling":0,"restart":"best","kick":0,"weight":40}]}. Reason: concentrate the fixed budget on immediate savings. Compare against baseline and the escape policy on shared workloads.
hypotheses.mechanism: Biasing moves toward expensive incoming transitions targets avoidable setup time, while relocation, swap and reversal inspect complementary directed-cycle improvements.

hypotheses.claim: Nearest-neighbor schedules occupy local basins; bounded escape followed by polishing can exceed a mean absolute cost_reduction of 0.02 and outperform greedy-only search.
hypotheses.experiment: Use an escape assembly policy matched to the greedy policy in operators, sampling, stage weights and total evaluations, changing only first-stage acceptance and initialization. Executable reference program: {"stages":[{"operators":["relocate","swap"],"sampling":"expensive","acceptance":"anneal","temperature":0.03,"cooling":1,"restart":"kick","kick":2,"weight":60},{"operators":["relocate","swap","reverse"],"sampling":"scan","acceptance":"improve","temperature":0,"cooling":0,"restart":"best","kick":0,"weight":40}]}. Reason: test whether escaping a basin justifies spending evaluations on non-improving states. Attribute any contrast to the combined escape intervention, not separately to annealing or kicks.
hypotheses.mechanism: A small perturbation and temporary uphill acceptance permit coordinated changes unavailable to strictly improving trajectories; restoring the best cycle before polishing preserves discovered savings.

model_plan.objective: Reduce total directed setup minutes per repeating production cycle relative to the current engine, while visiting every job exactly once, starting and ending at job 0, and limiting each search to 256 candidate-cost evaluations.

instruction.instruction: Use the measured planning feedback to propose two distinct bounded search programs that reduce setup costs on new workloads. Consider the choice and ordering of search operations, exploration and acceptance. Explain each hypothesis briefly.
